title: Tenant affinity loss during API gateway redeploy causing misattributed billing
creator: Priya Patel
description: Summary: During a recent API gateway redeploy (zero-downtime rolling update) we observed sustained misattribution of token usage to a single org/project. The spike correlated with gateway pod restarts and a downstream connection pool behavior that appears to preserve stale tenant metadata on recycled upstream connections. Impact: incorrect billing and rate-limiter enforcement for affected customers; multiple small orgs saw their usage billed to a single project for ~3 hours. Goal: identify root cause, implement a robust fix to prevent per-connection tenant affinity leakage, and run reconciliation to correct historical attribution.
reproduce_steps: 1) Provision two test projects (Project-A / Project-B) each with their own API key. 2) Start steady parallel traffic from both keys against the gateway (1rps per key) for 30 minutes. 3) Trigger a rolling redeploy of the api-gateway image with existing keepalive settings (graceful drain). 4) Observe usage dashboards: look for a sudden collapse of Project-B tokens and corresponding increase in Project-A's billed tokens. 5) Tail gateway debug logs (X-Forwarded-For, X-Org-ID headers, connection pooled upstream selection). Expected: each request's tenant should be present in per-request header and the upstream should charge the correct tenant. Actual: many upstream requests carry the wrong X-Org-ID header or upstream context that matches previously served tenant on that connection.
hypothesis: Primary hypothesis: the gateway's upstream connection pool caches a per-connection mapped header (X-ORG-ID or internal tenant header) when a connection is first populated; when connections are reused across different incoming requests (keepalive / pooling) the code fails to overwrite or clear the tenant-scoped header. A secondary hypothesis: long-lived gRPC streams between gateway and runtime worker carry attached metadata that is not reset when the logical tenant context changes due to connection reuse or proxy sticky routing. Both lead to the backend attribution layer seeing the wrong org id and incrementing the wrong billing counters and rate-limit buckets.
mitigation_short_term: 1) Immediately disable aggressive upstream connection reuse on gateway pods handling multi-tenant traffic (set keepalive: short / max_connections_per_host=1) in staging and a small subset of production to validate. 2) Enable additional request-level logging to capture request_id, api_key_id, observed X-Org-ID, and upstream connection_id for forensic correlation. 3) Kick off a one-off reconciliation job to reassign misattributed usage for the 3-hour window using request traces and raw ingress logs. 4) Notify affected customers and support with temporary credits until reconciliation completes.
proposed_fix: 1) Fix gateway connection pooling to avoid caching tenant-scoped headers on a per-connection basis. Ensure per-request header injection is performed for each request and any per-connection metadata is cleared on reuse. 2) Add a defensive assertion in the runtime ingress that validates api_key -> org mapping for every request; if mismatch is detected, reject or log at error level and route to a safe fallback. 3) Harden gRPC metadata handling: do not reuse stream metadata for new logical requests. 4) Add unit and integration tests that simulate connection reuse under key rotations and gateway redeploys.
qa_tests: - Unit tests: mock upstream connection pool; assert header cleared before reuse. - Integration: staging test with two projects under sustained traffic and multiple redeploy cycles; assert no cross-tenant attribution. - Load test: ramp to 500rps with randomized API key set and run a rolling update; verify billing counters remain stable per-tenant. - Regression: add fuzz test around key rotations + rolling gateway restarts to reproduce historical failure mode.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge gateway fix behind feature flag. 2) Deploy to canary cluster (1 pod) and run e2e staging tests for 6 hours. 3) If green, expand to 10% of prod traffic for 24 hours while running reconciliation dry-run. 4) Gradual 100% rollout with monitoring alerts and rollback playbook. 5) Post-deploy: run a reconciliation job for the affected window and publish customer-facing postmortem and credits where required.
